articleBlocks: The first four clues look like a straightforward animation category: Tweety, Pac-Man, SpongeBob, and Bart are all famous cartoon figures. That surface read invites 'cartoon characters' or 'animated icons' as the answer, which feels plausible until the last clue. The Minions clue adds a rhyme hint, 'rhymes with Bello!', which does not fit a genre label like animation or mascots. That hint points to a single word that sounds like 'Bello' and quietly changes the filter from medium to color.
Once color becomes the filter, every earlier clue snaps into place as a yellow character rather than just a cartoon.
Tweety is a yellow canary, Pac-Man is a yellow circle, SpongeBob is a yellow sponge, and Bart has yellow skin.
The Minions themselves are yellow henchmen, so the rhyme hint confirms the color without ever printing the answer.
The puzzle misleads by stacking five recognizable animation names, which makes the broad category feel complete before the last clue.
The final reading is cleaner because it uses one shared visual trait that applies to all five clues equally.
That trait is not just 'yellow things' but specifically fictional characters whose canonical design is yellow.
The rhyme hint is the only clue that breaks the genre read, and it does so by pointing directly at the color word.
In hindsight, the set is a tight color category disguised as a list of famous cartoons.
The answer was Fictional characters that are yellow.
